recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片三格組圖中（箭頭處），多顆漿細胞的胞質被一顆顆淡藍灰色的圓形小球填滿，像一串葡萄、把核遮住或推到一側；胞質內滿是 Russell body 的 Mott cell，本例見於漿細胞骨髓瘤。
features: Multiple plasma cells with cytoplasm packed by numerous pale blue-gray, round, uniform globules (Russell bodies), giving a grape-cluster or morula appearance
Nuclei round, eccentric, with clumped chromatin, partly obscured by the inclusions
Mott cells occur singly and in small groups (arrowheads)
Admixed conventional plasma cells, maturing granulocytes, and erythroid precursors
Stretched nuclear strand and a few smudged cells in the bottom panel are smearing artifacts
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear (three fields) shows numerous Mott cells, plasma cells whose cytoplasm is distended by multiple round, pale blue-gray globular inclusions (Russell bodies) that partially obscure eccentric nuclei with clumped chromatin. Conventional plasma cells are also present, admixed with maturing granulocytic and erythroid precursors. Russell bodies represent accumulated immunoglobulin within dilated endoplasmic reticulum. Mott cells are not specific for malignancy; in this context the findings are consistent with plasma cell myeloma, and plasma cell percentage and light-chain restriction should be established.

ddx.vs: Morphology alone cannot separate them; reactive states show polytypic kappa/lambda expression and fewer plasma cells without an M-protein.
Dutcher bodies are single intranuclear-appearing PAS-positive inclusions overlying the nucleus, rather than multiple cytoplasmic globules.
These are giant azurophilic or dense granules in granulocytes/blasts, not pale uniform globules filling plasma cell cytoplasm.
Histiocytes are larger with small central nuclei and crumpled-tissue-paper or foamy cytoplasm, lacking plasma cell nuclear features.
